title: Substitute u = e^(kt) to turn an equation with a repeated exponential term into a quadratic
content: When an equation contains both e^(kt) and e^(-kt) (or e^(2kt)) terms, multiply through so every exponential term is written as a power of the same base term, then let u = e^(kt). This converts the equation into an ordinary quadratic in u. Solve the quadratic, reject any root that is zero or negative (since e^(kt) > 0 for all real t), then take logs of the remaining positive root to solve for t.
